{{short description|German chemist (1933–2025)}}
'''Hartmut Bärnighausen''' (16 February 1933 – 30 March 2025) was a German chemist and [[Crystallography|crystallographer]]. He was known for establishing the [[Bärnighausen trees]] which describe group-subgroup relationships of crystal structures.<ref name="Bronger-2003">{{Cite journal|last=Bronger|first=W.|last2=Dehnicke|first2=K.|last3=Hanke|first3=W.|date=2003|title=Gratulation: Professor Hartmut Bärnighausen zum 70. Geburtstag am 16. Februar 2003|journal=Zeitschrift für Anorganische und Allgemeine Chemie|language=en|volume=629|issue=3|pages=363–364|doi=10.1002/zaac.200390058|issn=1521-3749}}</ref>

== Life ==
Bärnighausen studied Chemistry at [[Leipzig University]] and received his diploma after a diploma thesis with [[Leopold Wolf]] in 1955.<ref name="Bronger-2003" /> In May 1958, he flew from [[East Germany]] to [[University of Freiburg]], where he worked with [[Georg Brauer]].<ref name="Bronger-2003" /> He finished his doctorate in the group of [[Georg Brauer]] in 1959.<ref name="Bronger-2003" /> In 1967, he received his habilitation.<ref name="Bronger-2003" /> From 1967 to 1998, he was a professor for inorganic chemistry at the [[University of Karlsruhe]].<ref name="Bronger-2003" />

Bärnighausen died on 30 March 2025, at the age of 92.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Remembering Hartmut Bärnighausen: Architect of the Group–Subgroup Approach in Crystallography |url=https://www.iucr.org/news/newsletter/volume-33/number-3/hartmut-barnighausen-1933-2025 |access-date=2025-09-22 |website=www.iucr.org}}</ref>

== Research ==
His research focused on the following topics:

* crystallographic group theory in [[crystal chemistry]] ([[Bärnighausen trees]])<ref name="Bronger-2003" />
* synthesis and characterization of new compounds in including rare earth metals<ref name="Bronger-2003" />
* structure refinements of twinned crystals<ref name="Bronger-2003" />

== Awards ==
He was awarded the [[Carl Hermann Medal]] of the [[German Crystallographic Society]] in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dgk-home.de/en/society/honorary-members-and-award-winner/winner-of-the-carl-hermann-medal/|title=Winners of the Carl-Hermann-Medal {{!}} Deutsche Gesellschaft für Kristallographie|website=dgk-home.de|access-date=2018-12-21}}</ref>
